title: Prime Matrix Serialization
objective: Optimize public SagePack serialization and deserialization for packed dense GF(p) matrices with exact format compatibility, host-independent bulk transfers, malformed-input validation, ownership safety, and warm benchmark gates

oracles: public Sage.js round-trip and malformed-input behavior
exceptions: The stable SagePack envelope is implemented in TypeScript at the host serialization boundary; this lane adds no handwritten native mathematics and keeps packed GF(p) storage canonical.

handoff.summary: Replaced per-entry BigInt shifts in the portable uint64 SagePack primitives with endian-aware typed-array bulk paths; skipped redundant built-in codec dispatch only for codec-produced payload records; and validated/decoded packed prime residues directly into fresh canonical Matrix storage. GF(97) 500x500 warm SagePack improved from roughly 22-37 ms serialization and 7-12 ms deserialization to about 1.5-1.7 ms and 1.7-3.0 ms respectively, while preserving the existing golden bytes. Bootstrap changes are confined to rho-sigma uint64_pack_le and uint64_unpack_le.
risks: The explicit big-endian fallback is covered by byte-pattern oracles but was not executed on physical big-endian CI hardware.
next_steps: Integrate before the dynamic FFI cache lane, which must preserve the two updated bootstrap uint64 primitive bodies when rebasing.
